title: Seasonal change table
subject: Science
unit: Summer 1: Ecosystems (7D); atoms, elements and molecules (7H)
source: Seeded from science/y7 lesson 52 (Seasonal change table (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 52: Adapting to daily and seasonal change. To understand how organisms cope with changes in their environment over a day and a year

questions.a: Their prey (moths) fly at night and there is less competition and fewer predators
questions.model: Ask: what does the bat eat, and when is it about? Moths at night. Being nocturnal lets it catch them with less competition.

questions.a: Moving to another place for part of the year

questions.q: Give one reason an oak drops its leaves.
questions.a: Less light in winter / water hard to get

questions.q: Make a 'year in the life' table for a hedgehog and an oak tree: spring, summer, autumn, winter.
questions.a: Seasonal changes correct, e.g. hedgehog fattens in autumn, hibernates in winter; oak leaves fall in autumn, buds in spring
questions.model: Teacher fills the hedgehog's autumn box: 'eats lots to build fat stores'.

questions.q: Keep a 3-day log of a living thing you can see from home (morning and evening).
How might warmer winters affect hibernating animals?
questions.a: They may wake early when food is still scarce

questions.q: Big question: why do swallows migrate?
questions.a: Their insect food is scarce in a British winter, so they go where food is.
